question.text: Per the chapter, a PRIMARY reason why Mark-to-Market on a daily basis is 'crucial' for Cat III AIFs is:

answer.text: To compute the Fair Value of portfolio, reconcile margins with brokers, and determine fair Incentive Fees and fair redemption NAV
To eliminate the need for a valuer

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'Since Category III AIFs invest in derivative contracts, it becomes essential for the Investment Manager to follow Daily Mark-to-Market process, for reconciliation of margin accounts with brokers and representing a Fair Value of the Portfolio... Mark-to-Market process is crucial for the Investment Manager and investors, to determine the fair amount of Incentive Fees payable.' The Trap: Auditor/tax/valuer-elimination are false - MTM is complementary to all these. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B, XIX-C, VIII and XXI-B all test MTM's multiple purposes. Manager's Pro-Tip: Run daily MTM reconciliation between broker file and internal P&L by 7 pm IST - any unexplained delta > INR 1 lakh goes into a daily break-report reviewed by the CRO. Over a year this discipline prevents the classic month-end NAV shock.
